finding.claim: [PLAUSIBLE, needs live test] A client-controlled Connection header can strip Content-Length from the upstream request (strip_connection_tokens removes any connection-listed name not in the static list), and CL+TE requests are never rejected. The forwarded body framing may then disagree with what the backend expects on a pooled upstream connection, enabling request smuggling/desync. Whether this is exploitable depends on how Pingora frames upstream requests with no CL/TE.
finding.source: Client request headers: `Connection: content-length` on a POST with a body, or `Content-Length` together with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`. Entry: request_filter/mod.rs:70 normalize_request_headers.
finding.sink: Upstream request header set built in upstream_request_filter (with_body.rs:209-222), which determines the framing of the forwarded body on a reused upstream connection.

trace.note: SINGLE_VALUE_HEADERS covers only Content-Length and Content-Type; no Transfer-Encoding check.
normalize_request_headers runs only duplicate CL/CT and obs-fold checks. No CL+TE conflict check.
normalize is called on every request; nothing after it checks framing headers.
upstream_request_filter calls strip_hop_by_hop on the upstream request.
strip_hop_by_hop removes REQUEST_HOP_BY_HOP (which includes transfer-encoding) and then calls strip_connection_tokens.
REQUEST_HOP_BY_HOP does not include content-length.
Any Connection token not in the static list is removed, so `Connection: content-length` removes CL from the upstream request.
apply_mutated_content_length re-adds CL only when a body writer mutated the body, so the stripped CL is not restored.

finding.guards_checked: Present: duplicate CL/CT conflict rejection (normalize.rs:75-99); obs-fold rejected on CL and Host (normalize.rs:141-149); reserved-header rejection (request_filter/mod.rs:75); TE removed from the upstream request by the static list. Missing: CL+TE rejection (RFC 9112 6.3), protection of CL from Connection-token stripping. Unverified: Pingora's upstream framing when neither CL nor TE is present.

finding.claim: [PLAUSIBLE, depends on admin_addr exposure] The admin listener exposes unauthenticated KV read, list-all, write and delete. Anyone who can reach admin_addr can modify KV stores that filters may use for policy, and can read every value by listing a store.
finding.source: Any network client that can reach admin_addr: GET/PUT/DELETE /api/kv/{store}[/{key}].
finding.sink: KvStoreRegistry backend set / delete / entries (kv/mod.rs:169-190, 193-211), via the same listener that serves /metrics and /ready.

trace.note: PingoraAdminService::response dispatches /api/kv/* with no auth check.
Path prefix /api/kv/ is routed straight to dispatch_kv_request when a KV registry exists.
dispatch_kv_request has no authentication or source-address check.
resolve_kv_route accepts PUT and DELETE from any caller.
read_body enforces the 1 MiB cap and UTF-8 check, and nothing else.
handle_set writes the attacker-chosen value into the store.
handle_list returns every key and value in the store.
add_admin_endpoints_to_pingora_server binds admin_addr as plain TCP with no TLS and no auth; the bind address comes from operator config, which is not in this repo.

finding.guards_checked: Present: 1 MiB body cap (kv/mod.rs:25,129); UTF-8 validation (kv/mod.rs:142); store capacity limit (kv/mod.rs:176); JSON escaping of keys and values (kv/mod.rs:159-160, 202-203); 404 for unknown stores. Missing: any authentication or authorization, TLS, and source restriction in this crate. Not verifiable here: admin_addr default and whether filters use KV for authz decisions.

finding.claim: [PLAUSIBLE, relies on Pingora insert_header replacing all values] obs-fold unfolding calls insert_header(name, new_value) for each folded value. That replaces every value for that header name, so unfolded-away sibling values are silently discarded. A client can make a trusted header set by an upstream load balancer disappear and leave only a client-chosen value, which the backend may then trust (for example, spoofed X-Forwarded-For).
finding.source: Client sends a folded header (CRLF followed by SP/HTAB) such as `X-Forwarded-For: 1.1.1.1\r\n 2.2.2.2`. A trusted LB in front of praxis appends its own X-Forwarded-For line with the real client IP.
finding.sink: req_header_mut().insert_header in handle_obs_fold; the surviving value is forwarded to the backend (with_body.rs:209-226).

trace.note: handle_obs_fold builds headers_snapshot from folded entries only; sibling values are excluded.
Loop over the snapshot.
insert_header replaces all existing values for the name with the single unfolded value.
normalize_request_headers runs before the filter pipeline, so filters and the backend see the rewritten set.

finding.guards_checked: Present: obs-fold rejected on Host and Content-Length (normalize.rs:141-149). Not checked: whether a folded header has other same-name values. Verify that Pingora RequestHeader::insert_header replaces all values, not just the first.

finding.claim: [CONFIRMED in code] OPTIONS and TRACE requests with `Max-Forwards: 0` are answered directly before any filter in the pipeline runs. Auth, IP allow/deny, rate-limit and other policy filters are skipped, and response-phase filters (security headers, body filters) are also skipped. Impact is limited: the response is a 200 with no backend data, but policy filters are bypassed and the 200 acts as an oracle for requests that policy would have denied.
finding.source: Any client, unauthenticated, sending `OPTIONS /protected` or `TRACE /protected` with `Max-Forwards: 0`.
finding.sink: send_rejection(Rejection::status(200) or TRACE echo) in validation.rs:121, which writes directly to the session without running the pipeline.

trace.note: handle_max_forwards runs before run_pipeline (line 133) and before body pre-read, so no policy filter has run yet.
Method gate: only TRACE and OPTIONS.
mf == 0 branch.
send_rejection writes the response directly.
send_rejection writes headers and body straight to the session; no response filters run.

finding.guards_checked: Present: Host validation (validation.rs:30-44), obs-fold and duplicate-header normalization, and reserved-header rejection all run before Max-Forwards handling. Connection limits (with_body.rs:127-148) still apply. Missing: any policy check before the short-circuit.

finding.sink: Path matching in the router and ACL filters (praxis_filter, not in this repo); the final upstream URI is set at upstream_request.rs:108.

The unnormalized Request is built here.
run_pipeline evaluates filters against this request.
Only the rewritten path is validated (lines 79-105); the inbound path is never canonicalized.

finding.guards_checked: Present: dot-dot and %2e%2e checks, scheme/authority rejection and leading-slash checks on rewritten paths only (upstream_request.rs:79-105, tests 566-587). Missing: any canonicalization of the inbound path. Verify against praxis_filter's router and ACL matching.

finding.claim: [LOW, design-level, may be intended] Once an upstream answers a valid WebSocket 101, connection_upgraded is set and request/response body filters are skipped for the rest of the connection. Body-level size limits and body policy then stop applying to later frames. The client chooses the upgrade, but the upstream must accept it.
finding.source: Client sends `Upgrade: websocket` with `Connection: Upgrade` to an endpoint whose upstream accepts WebSocket.
finding.sink: Early return in request_body_filter (request_body_filter.rs:41-43) and the response body hooks, which skip processing.

trace.note: Unsolicited 101 is rejected unless the request carried Upgrade.
is_upgrade_response requires a websocket Upgrade value.
ctx.connection_upgraded set.
Request body hook returns early when connection_upgraded is set.

finding.guards_checked: Present: unsolicited 101 rejected (response_filter.rs:40-46); requires Upgrade: websocket and sec-websocket-accept (response_filter.rs:204-210); h2c stripped (hop_by_hop.rs:61-63). Missing: any policy check on frames after upgrade.

finding.source: Client request body of any size, when the pipeline reports BodyMode::Stream.

match on ctx.request_body_mode.
Stream arm is empty: no size check.

finding.claim: [LOW, precondition outside this repo] The HTTP upstream path resolves hostnames and builds a peer without any private/reserved-address check and without reading allow_private_upstreams. The TCP path enforces that check. This matters only if a filter derives an upstream from client-controlled input (Host, SNI, path).
finding.source: Upstream address from config. Client-controlled only if a filter (outside this repo) maps client input to an upstream address.
finding.sink: HttpPeer::new(addr, tls, sni) at upstream_peer.rs:67, connecting to the resolved address.

build_peer resolves the address.
resolve_address delegates to peer_utils::resolve_address (praxis_core, not in this repo) with no private check here.
The TCP path rejects private/reserved resolved IPs unless allow_private_upstreams is set.
